from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Ternary systems utilize three states: zero, one, two.",
            "Three states naturally represent transitions between three locations.",
            "Base-three counting simplifies Hanoi Tower movement patterns."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Base-3 Intuition", lecture_lines)

        colors = ["#FF5733", "#33FF57", "#3357FF"]
        disks = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.5, color=c, fill_opacity=0.7) for c in colors])
        labels = VGroup(*[Text(f"Size {i}", font_size=16) for i in range(3)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(disks.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Position disks
        self.place_at_grid(disks[0], "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(disks[1], "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(disks[2], "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Label them
        for i in range(3):
            self.place_at_grid(labels[i], f"{['B', 'C', 'D'][i]}4", scale_factor=1.0)
            self.play(Write(labels[i]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Shift disks to simulate transition
        self.play(
            disks[0].animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]),
            disks[1].animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]),
            disks[2].animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))
        self.play(
            *[disk.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF") for disk in disks],
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Constrained Towers of Hanoi", [
            "Disks move only between adjacent pegs in this variation.",
            "Moving three disks requires exactly twenty-six steps.",
            "The move count follows the pattern three to n minus one."
        ])
        
        # Prepare peg visualization
        pegs = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(3)])
        self.place_at_grid(pegs[0], "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(pegs[1], "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(pegs[2], "B6")
        
        # Connections
        line_ab = Line(pegs[0].get_right(), pegs[1].get_left(), color=WHITE)
        line_bc = Line(pegs[1].get_right(), pegs[2].get_left(), color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pegs), Create(line_ab), Create(line_bc))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent disks as rectangles on peg A
        disks = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=0.2, width=0.8-i*0.15, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1) for i in range(3)])
        disks.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.05).next_to(pegs[0], UP, buff=0.1)
        self.add(disks)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        # Highlight constrained paths
        self.play(Indicate(line_ab, color="#FFFF00"), Indicate(line_bc, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Moves to the Sierpinski Triangle", [
            "Map disk configurations to points on a triangle graph.", 
            "Legal moves represent edges between adjacent sub-triangles.", 
            "The entire state space forms a Sierpinski triangle."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        triangle = Triangle(color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(triangle, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=2.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(triangle))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualizing mapping to sub-triangles
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=triangle.get_vertices()[i]) for i in range(3)])
        self.play(Create(dots))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Drawing recursive structure representation
        sub_triangles = VGroup(
            Triangle(color=BLUE).scale(0.5).move_to(triangle.get_center() + UP*0.5),
            Triangle(color=BLUE).scale(0.5).move_to(triangle.get_center() + LEFT*0.4 + DOWN*0.3),
            Triangle(color=BLUE).scale(0.5).move_to(triangle.get_center() + RIGHT*0.4 + DOWN*0.3)
        )
        self.play(Create(sub_triangles))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *

class SierpinskiTriangle(VGroup):
    def __init__(self, order=3, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        triangle = Polygon(LEFT+DOWN, RIGHT+DOWN, UP, color=BLUE)
        self.add(triangle)
        self.order = order
        for _ in range(order):
            new_triangles = VGroup()
            for tri in self:
                vertices = tri.get_vertices()
                p1, p2, p3 = vertices[0], vertices[1], vertices[2]
                m1 = (p1 + p2) / 2
                m2 = (p2 + p3) / 2
                m3 = (p3 + p1) / 2
                new_triangles.add(Polygon(p1, m1, m3, color=BLUE))
                new_triangles.add(Polygon(m1, p2, m2, color=BLUE))
                new_triangles.add(Polygon(m3, m2, p3, color=BLUE))
            self.submobjects = new_triangles.submobjects

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Ternary numbers serve as precise path coordinates.",
            "Incrementing ternary values dictates optimal movement sequences.",
            "This recursive harmony guides paths through the fractal."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Synthesis: Recursive Harmony", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Overlay triangle structure onto [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg]
        tower = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg")
        triangle = SierpinskiTriangle(order=3)
        
        self.place_in_area(tower, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(triangle, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(tower))
        self.play(Create(triangle))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate recursive moves following the Sierpinski path
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'B3')
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        path = VMobject().set_points_smoothly([self.grid['B3'], self.grid['E4'], self.grid['C5'], self.grid['B3']])
        path.set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(dot, path), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Synthesize final state
        self.play(triangle.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), dot.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), tower.animate.set_opacity(0.3))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Ternary Bridge: From Hanoi Towers to the Sierpinski Triangle
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: The Base-3 Intuition
sections.content: Introduce the ternary system (0, 1, 2) as a natural language for systems with three states. Explain why ternary is the optimal representation for processes involving transitions between three distinct locations.
sections.example: Representing a ternary counter using three colors of light bulbs (Red=0, Green=1, Blue=2) changing states.

sections.title: Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Discuss the 'Frame-Stewart' or 'Adjacency Constraint' variation: disks can only move to adjacent pegs (A↔B, B↔C). Show that the minimum move count for n disks is 3^n - 1, establishing a direct link between ternary counting and recursive moves.
sections.example: A robotic arm moving three disks between three pegs arranged in a circle, where the 'jump' between peg A and C is forbidden.

sections.title: Mapping Moves to the Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Visualize the state space of the constrained Hanoi problem. Show how every legal configuration of disks maps to a point on a Sierpinski triangle graph. Each move corresponds to traversing an edge between sub-triangles.
sections.example: An animation showing a disk configuration tree unfolding into a geometric fractal triangle as the number of disks increases.

sections.title: The Synthesis: Recursive Harmony
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts: Ternary numbers act as coordinates in the Sierpinski triangle. By incrementing a ternary number, we precisely dictate the path required to solve the Hanoi puzzle, effectively navigating the fractal graph.
sections.example: Using a ternary counter (00, 01, 02, 10...) to guide a 'turtle' bot tracing the exact path along a Sierpinski gasket.
